elements.text: Give urgent attention to the patient with suicidal thoughts or behaviour 34.
LOW MOOD, STRESS OR ANXIETY
Assess the patient with low mood, stress or anxiety. If patient known with depression, give routine depression care instead 160.
Assess Note

Anxiety • If excessive worry causes impaired function/distress for at least 6 months with ≥ 3 of: muscle tension, restlessness, irritability, difficulty sleeping, poor concentration, tiredness, generalised anxiety disorder likely 160. • If anxiety is induced by a particular situation/object (phobia) or is repeated sudden fear with physical symptoms and no obvious cause (panic), discuss/refer. • If anxiety > 1 month linked to a bad experience, with ≥ 3 of: nightmares/flashbacks, avoids situations/people, constantly on guard/easily startled, feels numb/detached from others/surroundings, post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) likely. Discuss/refer.
Depression In the past month, has patient felt down/depressed/hopeless or little interest/pleasure in doing things? If yes to either 159.
Substance use In the past year, has patient drunk ≥ 4 drinks1/session, used illegal drugs or misused prescription or over-the-counter medications? If yes to any 165.
Abuse If patient is being abused 33.

Stressors • Help identify psychosocial stressors. Ask about family or relationship problems, infertility, financial difficulty, bereavement, chronic ill-health. If sexual problems 74. • If patient has a life-limiting illness, in bed or chair for 50% or more of the day or dependent on others for most care, also give palliative care 191. • If older person, ask about loneliness and if available, refer to nearest social club for older people in the area.

Women’s health • If recent delivery, give postnatal care 182 and if available, refer to mother's support group. • If woman > 40 years, ask about menopausal symptoms: hot flushes, night sweats, vaginal dryness, mood changes, difficulty sleeping and sexual problems 74.
Medication Review medication: prednisone, efavirenz, metoclopramide, theophylline and contraceptives can cause mood changes. Discuss with doctor. Consider alternative contraceptive 187.

Advise the patient with low mood, stress or anxiety • Refer to social worker, occupational therapist, counsellor or psychiatric nurse/psychologist. Encourage supportive family member/friend to attend follow up visits as well. • Encourage patient to question negative thinking and be realistic if s/he often predicts the worst, exaggerates problem, inappropriately takes the blame, takes things personally. • Help patient to choose strategies to get help and cope:
Limit alcohol and avoid drugs • Limit alcohol to ≤ 2 drinks/ day if man and 1 drink/day if woman. • Avoid drugs.
Get enough sleep
If patient has difficulty sleeping,
give advice 99.
Access support Link patient with helpline or support group 200.
Get active Do some enjoyable physical activity
Do a relaxing breathing exercise each day.
Spend time with supportive
friends or family.
Find a creative or fun activity to do.
Encourage patient to take time to relax:

• Deal with bereavement issues if patient or family member has a life-limiting illness or if patient is recently bereaved: - Acknowledge grief reactions: denial, disbelief, confusion, shock, sadness, bargaining, yearning, anger, humiliation, despair, guilt and acceptance. - Allow patient/family to share sorrow and talk of memories, the meaning of the patient’s life or religious beliefs. Suggest connecting with a spiritual counsellor as appropriate. - Identify worrying issues (e.g. child care, will and funeral arrangements) and who can give practical support with these before and after the patient dies. • For tips on how to communicate effectively 198.
Review the patient every 2-4 weeks. If no improvement after 3 months, assess for depression/anxiety 159.
1One drink is 1 tot of spirits, or 1 small glass (125mL) of wine or 1 can/bottle (330mL) of beer.
